Second in the series of “handle with care”, I made a hexagonal matrix flash light. It’s controlled by @adafruit Trinket M0 and powered by a small LiPo.

 I wrote a simple code in Arduino for the onboard @adafruit Trinket M0. The LEDs are driven by three MOSFETs and powered by a small LiPo. The LEDs together consume around 5W peak.

I used a 3D printed hexagon matrix jig to solder the LEDs together. I uploaded the design on thingiverse. Look up “LED matrix soldering jig” if you are interested.

Each LED has a 10 ohm current limiting resistor. A total of 37 LEDs.

When simple shapes turn into fun forms 🛰️ I made a little solar powered “satellite” that transmits temperature and humidity data as BLE beacon packets. The heart of the build is the nRF52840 SoC dev board from @seeedstudio. I’m using a 50F 3.8V hybrid super capacitor, which is charged by couple of solar cells, to power the system. A fully charged capacitor powers the device for little over a month. More information and videos to follow!

New year, new lander. Meet Cumin!
videos.desc:
Cumin is a little lander built around the @seeedstudio XIAO nRF52840 dev board. It measures temperature, humidity, and pressure using a BME280 sensor and displays it on a 128x32 OLED. The whole thing is powered by a single 14250 Lithium Ion battery.

videos.t: Setting time on the Cumin Lander over BLE #arduino #circuitsculpture
videos.desc: Setting time on Cumin Lander over BLE. After the time is set, the nRF52840’s internal RTC takes over. I’m using the @adafruit Bluefruit app which opens up a UART interface over BLE on the device. Going to add more features using this technique! What should we do next?

It’s always fun to see how a simple, mundane circuit can be completely transformed when reimagined as a three dimensional circuit sculpture. How would you reimagine it?✨

This is a little lander sculpture I built around the nRF52840 based dev board. It measures temperature, humidity, and pressure. It displays that on a 128x32 OLED module along with time. The BLE connection allows me to configure the device remotely. Build tutorial coming up soon on my website! 🙏🏼🚀

videos.t: Pepper’s Ghost using a beam splitting cube #peppersghost #holocube #esp32 #hologram #cyberpunk
videos.desc: A simple pepper's ghost demonstration using a beam splitting prism cube and a 240x240 TFT display.

These little prisms are so much fun! They can transform any small, high-resolution screen into a floating display using the classic Pepper’s ghost effect—though, let’s be honest, it’s not really a hologram.

I’m using a @seeedstudio Xiao ESP32S3 board to drive a 240x240 IPS TFT display over SPI. The 25mm beam-splitting cube? I picked it up on Amazon over a year ago and am finally putting it to good use! You can also find them on AliExpress if you’re curious.

Sure, you can buy a fully assembled desktop gadget using an ESP32 to do the same thing, but where’s the fun in that? 😅

Here’s the transformation of an old sculpture! 🌟 Originally powered by a supercapacitor, it’s now running on a chonky CR2477 coin cell. Lots of build tips along the way!

💡 About the original design:
The display is driven by a 74HC47 BCD-to-seven-segment decoder. Fun fact: before adopting hexadecimal characters (A, B, C, D, E, F), TI and Siemens used modified versions of the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 to represent 10–14, with 15 left as a blank. The 74HC4060 ripple counter at the base feeds the seven-segment decoder with BCD numbers for the display.
